reputable

REP-yuh-tuh-bul -- shares a root with 'reputation.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Reputable is having a good reputation; well-regarded and trustworthy.

Before booking the trip, she only considered tour companies with a reputable track record of safety.

Example

A patient wants a reputable surgeon, so she checks board certifications, reads years of patient reviews, and confirms the doctor has never faced a single malpractice complaint.

That well-regarded, trustworthy standing built up over time is what reputable describes. Unlike 'famous,' which just means widely known, reputable specifically means well-regarded and trusted.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

esteemed: Esteemed describes someone held in real admiration -- a feeling people have about a person. Reputable is about a track record: a reputable firm has earned steady public trust over time, whether or not anyone actively admires it.

legitimate: Legitimate means genuine and operating within the rules -- a real business, not a scam. A legitimate company may still be brand-new and unknown; a reputable one has gone further and built a good name over time.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

disreputable: not considered to be respectable or trustworthy

notorious: famous for some bad quality or deed

Where it sits · from narrow trust to real admiration

credible → reputable → respected

credible vs. reputable: Credible is narrower than reputable -- credible mainly means believable or trustworthy in a specific claim, while reputable describes an overall, long-standing good reputation.

respected vs. reputable: Respected can feel even stronger than reputable: reputable simply means trusted enough not to raise concern, while respected implies genuine admiration built over time.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-: again, repeatedly (Latin)

root — -put-: to think, to consider (Latin (putare))

suffix — -able: able to be, worthy of being (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together: Latin re- ('again, repeatedly') plus putare ('to think, consider') plus -able ('worthy of being') -- reputable describes someone worthy of being thought well of, again and again.

Use the root in a new word: disputable: Whether the referee's call was fair remained disputable long after the game ended.
